_readme: The 18 PostHog alerts, as data. Each carries the RETIRED DATADOG QUERY VERBATIM in
`replaces`, so re-promoting or re-tuning one is a config change and not archaeology.
`insightKey` names the source insight by its STABLE KEY in insights.json, never by its
display name. Names are written for a reader and get rewritten; keys do not. Pointing an
alert at a name meant that renaming a tile silently detached its alert.

alerts.name: AECi — Cron job failed (any daily/hourly job)

replaces.datadogMonitor: AECi — Algolia sync failed / Home stats compute failed / Data quality job failed / Retention prune failed (4 monitors)

alerts.runbook: docs/RUNBOOKS.md — the per-job runbook named by `failing_jobs`; /admin/system shows the matching job_runs row.

replaces.datadogMonitor: AECi — Data quality check found ERROR-severity issues (by check)

replaces.datadogMonitor: AECi — Linear reconciliation: persistent stuck requests

alerts.runbook: docs/RUNBOOKS.md — 'Algolia index drift / orphan sweep'. Either raise DEFAULT_SAFETY_CAP deliberately or find out why the index diverged that far.

alerts.runbook: docs/RUNBOOKS.md — 'Auth sign-in error rate'. Check the `reason` breakdown on the Auth board: link_invalid / missing_code / auth_not_configured point at three different causes.

alerts.name: AECi — Toxicity scoring outage (> 50% errors, 1 h)
alerts.runbook: docs/RUNBOOKS.md — 'Toxicity scoring outage'. Reviews still submit; they queue for human moderation without a score.

alerts.name: AECi — page_views write error rate > 10% (1 h)
alerts.runbook: docs/RUNBOOKS.md — 'page_views write errors'. Traffic keeps serving; the admin panel's traffic screen under-reports.

alerts.name: AECi — Linear pipeline failure rate > 50% (1 h)
alerts.runbook: docs/RUNBOOKS.md — 'Linear pipeline failure'. The every-15-minute reconciliation sweep is the backstop; this alert says the backstop is doing all the work.

alerts.name: AECi — Linear webhook HMAC failures > 3 (1 h)
alerts.runbook: docs/RUNBOOKS.md — 'Linear webhook HMAC failures'. Check LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET first; if it is current, this is unauthenticated traffic.

alerts.name: AECi — WAF rate-limit / challenge spike (> 2,000 / 1 h)
alerts.runbook: docs/waf-rate-limits.md for the rule expressions; docs/RUNBOOKS.md — 'WAF rate-limit spike'.

alerts.name: AECi — p95 detail page render > 1.5 s (1 h)
alerts.runbook: docs/RUNBOOKS.md — 'High p95 detail render'. Check the Traffic board tile 'Page speed spread — how many were fast, how many were slow' first: it needs no reconstruction and cannot be wrong.

alerts.name: AECi — Search-engine pings refused (> 90% over 72 h)
alerts._calculationIntervalNote: Daily, not the hourly default. The window is 72 h (AECI-1136), so an hourly check would re-read the same three days 24 times a day and email on each firing check. A refusal episode lasts days and nothing is lost while it runs (the buffer keeps the URLs and the drain retries once a day), so one email a day is enough.

replaces._note: NEW with AECI-826 — no Datadog predecessor. `aeci.indexnow.submit` shipped in AECI-236 and was never alerted on, which is why production sat at a 100% HTTP 429 failure rate for at least three days with nothing noticing. A fail-open integration with no ratio alert is indistinguishable from a healthy one.

alerts.name: AECi — Account record could not be created (any, 1 h)

replaces._note: NEW with AECI-1099, no Datadog predecessor. aeci.auth.profile_ensure shipped in AECI-770. Any outcome:failed is a user left with no profiles row, and a vendor with no profiles row cannot be seated.

alerts.runbook: docs/RUNBOOKS.md — 'Account record could not be created at sign-in'.

alerts.name: AECi — Emails failing to send (> 20% over 24 h, at least 2 failed)
alerts._calculationIntervalNote: Daily, not the hourly default. The window is 24 h, so an hourly check would re-read the same day 24 times and email on each firing check. Mail volume is two to four a day, so a shorter window would hold nothing to judge.

replaces._note: NEW with AECI-1206, no Datadog predecessor. aeci.email.send shipped with AECI-240 and was never alerted on. Threshold basis, production project 354071, 30 days to 2026-10-01: 6 sends, 0 failed, daily max 2, hourly max 1. Rate = (failed + unknown) / (sent + failed + unknown). unknown (AECI-1197 review) is a timeout or thrown call, so the mail may or may not have gone; it counts as failed in the numerator because the call did not complete. skipped, duplicate and suppressed made no Resend call and count on neither side. Two failures are needed before a rate is reported, so one failed send on a quiet day reads 0. A total outage still fires the same day: the two operator digests fail, 2 of 2 = 100%.

alerts.runbook: docs/email.md (Resend transport, domain verification, secrets); docs/NOTIFICATIONS.md for what each template is.

alerts.name: AECi — Far more emails than usual (> 50 in 24 h)
alerts._calculationIntervalNote: Daily, matching the 24 h window, for the same reason as email-failure-rate.

replaces._note: NEW with AECI-1206, no Datadog predecessor. Counts sent + failed, the sends that reached Resend. Threshold basis, production 30 days to 2026-10-01: 6 sends in total, daily p50 0, p95 2, max 2. The AECI-1199 digest tags add about 2 a day, so an expected day is 2 to 4. attestation-digest adds one per unmuted vendor_admin seat per day and no seats are granted yet. 50 is over ten times the busiest expected day and leaves room for about 40 seats. Revisit when seats are granted.

alerts.runbook: docs/NOTIFICATIONS.md names each template's sender; the email-sends-by-template tile shows which one burst.

alerts.name: AECi — Live site held back an email (any, 1 h)

replaces._note: NEW with AECI-1206, no Datadog predecessor. outcome:suppressed is the AECI-1198 tier delivery gate refusing an outside recipient. The gate applies to non-production tiers only, and only production reports to this project, so any count means the gate misread the tier and a real recipient got nothing. Production had never emitted the outcome as of 2026-10-01; it did not exist before this epic.
